name: Molex 4-pin peripheral power
description: The classic 4-pin PC peripheral power connector from the ATX PSU, long used for hard drives, optical drives, and fans. Carries +12V and +5V with two grounds between them. The shell is D-shaped/keyed so it only inserts one way. Colour code is standard: yellow=+12V, black=GND, red=+5V.

contacts.name: +12V
contacts.description: +12 V (yellow wire) -- motors, drive spindles, fans

variants: The pin order (12V, GND, GND, 5V) with the two rails on the OUTSIDE and grounds in the middle is standard. Colour code (yellow/black/black/red) is reliable on real PSUs.
SATA power (a flat 15-pin connector) has superseded this for drives, but Molex is still common on fans, older gear, and Molex-to-SATA/PCIe adapters.
gotchas: It is easy to force a Molex in slightly rotated or half-seated because the pins are chunky -- a partly-inserted connector can arc or make intermittent 12 V contact. Seat it fully and squarely.
Molex-to-SATA adapters are a known fire risk when cheaply molded (the crimp on the SATA side is the failure point). Prefer PSU-native SATA power over an adapter for a drive that draws real current.
12 V is on pin 1 and 5 V on pin 4 -- the rails are the two OUTER pins. Reversing your assumption (grounds outside) shorts a rail.
notes: Molex 8981 4-pin PC peripheral power (12V/GND/GND/5V, yellow/black/black/red). Universal PC standard.
